mode: New companion environment concept: imagined GitHub as a physical office
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / game environment concept.
Imagine GitHub itself as a REAL, welcoming, human-scale OFFICE, translated into the existing Copilot Hub low-poly game world. Create one beautiful landscape 16:9 interior image with a confident original composition. The user is exploring what GitHub would feel like as a physical workplace. This is an IMAGINED GitHub office, not a depiction of an existing real headquarters.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1 is a reference for the established ivory/indigo/teal art direction and architectural quality, NOT a composition to copy. Its enormous wall-size interface console must no longer dominate. We are now exploring a whole inhabitable office.
Image 2 is the actual Hub world style reference: matte low-poly geometry, broad daylight, faceted teal trees, modular white/blue-gray campus architecture. Preserve that one-world feeling.
Image 3 is the canonical Developer character for the small tower-inspection workbench only. Keep this orange character intact if shown.

THE IDEA: A PLACE TO BUILD TOGETHER.
Express GitHub spatially through shared making, branching ideas, discussion and quiet concentration. Design a plausible attractive office with varied spaces and thoughtful furniture. It should feel like people could sit down, review something, have coffee and build here. Warm and quietly inventive, not a spaceship bridge, data center, showroom, giant tablet or generic open-plan cubicle office.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION:
Wide architectural three-quarter interior view, slightly elevated from human eye level, showing the room's depth and multiple connected zones. Not a top-down floor plan. The central collaboration table and daylight dominate. A foreground furniture edge or low planter provides depth without blocking the view. Keep crisp stylized rendering throughout, no cinematic blur.
The physical ROOM occupies almost the entire picture. No full-screen UI overlay, no giant roster or stats panel taking over the composition. This is an environment study, with the previously designed Codex inspection functionality belonging to a normal-size workstation in the room.

FOCAL COLLABORATION AREA:
A beautifully simple communal worktable in pale natural oak, with two work surfaces joining into one rounded central discussion end, a subtle spatial metaphor for branches merging. Make the table ergonomic and realistically buildable, not a novelty sculpture. Thin charcoal legs and modest ivory cable trays; four or five understated low-poly chairs upholstered in muted lavender and blue-gray. Place only a few credible working objects: two open laptops with simple dark displays, a closed notebook, a mug, small desk lamp. No readable code or numerical dashboards. Leave generous clear table space.
Above it, a slender charcoal branching pendant carries a few warm-white circular light disks at its nodes, like an elegant git graph. Restrained architectural lighting, no neon tubes or glowing cable spaghetti.

GITHUB IDENTITY AS ARCHITECTURE:
One charcoal feature wall carries a small, accurately recognizable white GitHub Octocat mark and "GitHub" wordmark, engraved or mounted cleanly. Use this just once at a believable office-sign scale. This is the sole main brand sign, not a pattern of repeated logos.
Along this wall, a recessed contribution-inspired installation is made from small square acoustic/wood blocks in ivory, sage and deeper green, with subtly varied depths and an intentional clustered pattern. No dates, numbers, calendar labels, counters or live-data legend. It should read as tactile public artwork at first, with the GitHub reference revealed on closer inspection.
A modest low shelf and seating ledge below hold a few books and one plant. A small quiet "Copilot Hub" label can mark the tower workbench. No advertising slogans or wall-sized source code.

REVIEW AND FOCUS SPACES:
At one side, a small glass-fronted review room with slender dark framing, a round table and a simple board with a few colored sticky notes; a discreet etched "Review" on the glass. At the other side, a comfortable indigo/lavender window bench with a small side table provides a quiet focus nook. One ivory coffee cabinet supports a plain coffee machine and two cups. Show enough to suggest a functioning workplace without cluttering the scene.
Ceiling and walls use the Hub's layered ivory slabs, muted blue-gray framing, a few softly rounded corners and broad quiet color fields. Do not use bulky armored borders.

CONNECTION TO OUR GAME:
Large corner windows show recognizable nearby campus footpaths, simple benches and teal low-poly trees under soft daytime light. The view matches being inside the central Lab; no duplicate Lab outside.
A single human-scale tower-inspection workbench sits off to the right or rear as one part of the office: an ivory desk, slim indigo-backed alcove, a small physical plinth and the canonical orange Developer head hovering just above it. At most one compact side display shows abstract unnumbered visual meter shapes; avoid tiny unreadable UI copy. No giant floating controls. The workbench is plausibly reachable from a chair or standing position, not room-filling.
The Developer remains head only: faceted orange swept spikes, charcoal goggles with teal lenses, black face with exactly two cyan eye strokes, cream ear pods with curly-brace glyph. No new mascot body, no character redesign, no duplicate giant character.
Use established low-poly faceted plants and geometrically simple props, with well-scaled doorways, chair seats and desk heights.

PRIMER BRAND PALETTE AND MATERIALS:
Warm ivory architecture; near-black/charcoal sign and window frames; pale oak on table and a few shelf surfaces; indigo and lavender in textiles/acoustic accents; small teal details; sage/green only in plants and the contribution wall. Let color support architecture and warm daylight, not flood the room. Use Mona Sans-like clean typography for the very few signs.
Materials remain MATTE and game-stylized: flat solid colors, simple faceted shapes, subtle planar bevels and gentle contact shadows. Suggest wood with broad color and construction, not photographic grain. Clear glass can have a pale blue tint and simple clean reflection shapes.
Do not turn this into a photorealistic real-estate photograph, glossy science-fiction showroom or miniature toy diorama. It should look like a beautifully art-directed, believable office inside this exact low-poly game.

CONSTRAINTS:
No people or newly designed NPCs are necessary. Personal working objects make the office feel occupied.
No numerical stats, prices, counters, animation timelines, playback speed controls or transport controls. The environment study does not introduce new game functions or remove the previously approved inspection functions; it simply shows the room at office scale.
No presentation borders, annotations, material sample boards, concept titles, browser chrome or explanatory captions printed on the image. The result is one immersive interior scene, creative, coherent and clearly GitHub as a physical place.
